newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist leaders in new sleaze trial.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist leaders in new sleaze trial.

text.p: Two former treasurers of France's Socialist Party go on trial in the central city of Lyon on Monday over an allegedly illegal party fundraising scheme dating back to the late 1980s.
Henri Emmanuelli and Andre Laignel are among 50 defendants in a trial expected to last about a month. The others include numerous elected local Socialist officials and business executives.

Emmanuelli, who served as head of the Socialist Party after being its treasurer from 1988 until 1991, has already been convicted on similar charges in an earlier trial which took place in Brittany in 1995.

Emmanuelli was given a one-year suspended prison sentence and a 30,000 franc ($6,000) fine in May 1995 for receiving illicit campaign contributions from a front company known as the Urba consultancy company which was run by party insiders.
In the earlier trial, investigators uncovered a covert funding network used by the Socialists to finance their campaigns by taking rake-offs from public works contracts via such front companies.
The front companies allegedly demanded consulting fees from companies seeking public tenders, and part of that money was then funnelled to local Socialist candidates and the national party.
The trial beginning in Lyon on Monday is based on similar accusations, again involving the Urba consultancy firm, but this time involving party operations in the Mediterranean port city of Marseille.
Prosecutors say the party illegally raked off 9.4 million francs ($1.65 million) from public works contracts awarded in the region during 1988 and 1989.
Emmanuelli and Laignel, who are accused of receiving stolen goods and conspiracy to peddle influence, have said they were uninvolved in Urba and unaware of illegal activities.
But Urba's ex-chairman Gerard Monate has told investigators he worked with both men on contract awards and that all were aware of the improper dealings.

Emmanuelli, an unsuccessful contender for the Socialist presidential nomination as well as a former speaker of the French National Assembly, resigned his seat in parliament when he came under investigation in connection with Urba in 1992 but was later comfortably re- elected.
He was replaced as party leader by Lionel Jospin following Jospin's unsuccessful 1995 presidential campaign.
